newsitem.title: BOSNIA: ICRC responds to Serb charges over NATO arrest.
newsitem.headline: ICRC responds to Serb charges over NATO arrest.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Friday it was concerned by Bosnian Serb allegations that NATO soldiers may have misused a Red Cross symbol when arresting a war crimes suspect.
The ICRC did not confirm the allegations and said in a statement it was aware that the NATO-led peace Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia denied that it ever abused the symbol.

The wife of indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic accused SFOR on Thursday of carrying a Red Cross parcel into a hospital as a ruse to arrest its director, Milan Kovacevic, who is accused of complicity in genocide.
Ljiljana Karadzic, whose husband served as wartime political leader, heads the local Red Cross in Bosnia's Serb entity.
"The ICRC expresses its immediate concern about these allegations regarding the use of the Red Cross emblem," said the statement issued in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.
SFOR denied British soldiers had carried parcels with Red Cross symbols when they entered the hospital.

"My understanding is that SFOR soldiers entered the hospital and asked at reception the location of Kovacevic's office and they went to his office and detained him," SFOR spokesman Major Chris Riley told reporters.

The Geneva-based humanitarian organisation, which helps victims of war, noted the divergent account of events from SFOR and from Mrs Karadzic said it remained committed to operating as a neutral, impartial and independent organisation.
"In any event, the ICRC objects to any organisation using the Red Cross in a manner which jeopardises the neutrality and independence of the Red Cross movement."
The Bosnian Serb Red Cross is not one of the 171 national societies recognised by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), also based in Geneva.
The two umbrella groups form the International Red Cross Movement.
